assessment_summary: Individual assignment: This assignment aims to assist students’ development as an independent learner of the knowledge and skills acquired in this unit. Students are to select, analyse and submit a brief business report on a news item for a specific company relevant to this unit.

Group project report: The group project is an applied project aimed at assessing the knowledge acquired in this unit of study. Students will be required to demonstrate their critical thinking and analytical skills to analyse and recommend improvements to real-world businesses.

Group project presentation: The group project presentations are aimed at assessing the level of knowledge acquired in this unit of study. All group members must actively participate in the presentation.

Reflective journal: Individual continuous, reflective journal about the student’s authentic learning experience gleaned from the group project and the in-class activities. While the submission is due in W13, students are encouraged to reflect on weekly prompts by the teaching team, and can discuss their reflections in the weekly consultations. The final deliverable is a written reflective journal of 1500 words (± 10%).

Generative AI Strategy: By developing a clear strategy for using GenAI tools in assignment work, students will enhance their ability to leverage GenAI for tasks such as identifying literature, structuring ideas, refining text, and fact-checking while ensuring ethical and effective practices. The goal is not just to ensure academic integrity but also to reflect on how GenAI tools shape analytical and critical thinking skills. The deliverable is a 600 word (± 10%) document.
Detailed information for each assessment can be found on Canvas.

items.label: Overview paragraph 1
items.text: The rapid evolution and widespread adoption of digital technologies are transforming societies, economies, and the environment. These transformations bring significant benefits but also pose serious risks of harm, particularly for vulnerable and marginalised stakeholders, requiring a balanced approach that genuinely serves the common good. This unit unpacks the ethical dilemmas of sociotechnical change, exploring how digital technologies like artificial intelligence, blockchain, and social media impact privacy, equity, democracy, dignity, business, the environment, and more. Guided by compassion as a foundational principle, students will critically examine the ambiguous and pluralistic nature of digital innovations, developing the skills to manage ethical dilemmas and promote responsible digital innovation for the common good. The course integrates ethical theories with recent practical case studies, equipping students to address contemporary ethical dilemmas in today's digital world.

items.label: Learning outcome 1
items.text: LO1. Analyse the ethical challenges and paradoxes associated with digital innovations.

items.label: Learning outcome 2
items.text: LO2. Critically evaluate the societal, economic, and environmental impacts of digital technologies, considering both benefits and harms.

items.label: Learning outcome 3
items.text: LO3. Apply ethical frameworks and theories to navigate and resolve ethical dilemmas in digital innovation.

items.label: Learning outcome 4
items.text: LO4. Communicate and collaborate effectively on ethical issues in diverse professional contexts.

items.label: Learning outcome 5
items.text: LO5. Make informed decisions that balance technological progress with societal well-being and ethical integrity.
